news.Title: Stock Market Today, Sept. 4: Tesla Falls After Cybercab Launch Disappoints Investors
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), a global electric vehicle maker with energy storage and solar solutions, closed at $354.08, down 5.92%. Shares fell after the Cybercab launch underwhelmed investors, and investors are now watching the rollout and safety approvals.

Trading volume reached 64.4 million shares, coming in about 53% above its three-month average of 42.1 million shares. Tesla IPO'd in 2010 and has grown 22,169% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) closed at 7,718, down 0.38%, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) closed at 26,507, down 0.29%. Among automotive manufacturing peers, Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ:RIVN) closed at $15.74, down 1.07%, while General Motors (NYSE:GM) closed at $87.76, up 0.83%, highlighting mixed trading across electric-vehicle rivals.

What this means for investors

Today's trading made it clear that investors and analysts expected more from Tesla's Cybercab launch event in Austin last night. The invite-only event to showcase the purpose-built Cybercab robotaxi wasn't livestreamed, and CEO Elon Musk didn't make an appearance.

Details on the number of Cybercabs to be deployed and their locations were not provided, leading analysts to feel that the highly anticipated event offered little incremental information.

Tesla stock also pressured after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration launched an "audit query" to assess whether Tesla had correctly self-certified that the Cybercab is safe for public road use and meets the necessary federal safety standards.

The combined effect was that investors saw most of this week's gain in Tesla shares given back.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Tesla Inc. ( NASDAQ:TSLA ) fell 6.40% intraday, a day after it began offering rides in limited areas of Austin in the two-seater Cybercab, a vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals. The launch event was thin. Musk didn't attend, according to attendees, and executive remarks on pricing, manufacturing and technology ran about a quarter of an hour. Tesla wouldn't say when it will charge fares, though executives described dynamic pricing that rises with demand.

To add to the stock pressure, NHTSA opened an investigation into whether Tesla properly certified the vehicle, examining the process and technical data it used to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards for up to 1,000 Cybercabs. The agency noted the Cybercab lacks conventional manual controls including a steering wheel, brake pedal, accelerator pedal and mirrors. Automakers must certify their vehicles meet those standards.

Federal rules cap how many vehicles a manufacturer can sell without a steering wheel and pedals. Tesla had 420 autonomous vehicles registered in Texas as of Friday morning, 45 of them Cybercabs, against Waymo's 988. In California it holds no permits to run a robotaxi service or to test without a safety driver. NHTSA proposed in June to drop the manual brake pedal requirement, but said existing standards remain in force until that work is finished.

news.Title: Mizuho Resets Intel Target For the Rest of 2026
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Intel ( INTC ) just received a sharp price-target cut from Mizuho , but the reasoning behind the call is considerably more complicated than a straightforward bearish warning. Analyst Vijay Rakesh lowered his Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ) target to $92 from $109, a reduction of 15.6%, citing near-term multiple compression across agentic AI companies. He retained a Neutral rating, signaling that his concern centers on valuation and sentiment rather than a collapse in Intel's operating outlook. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with INTC. Is INTC fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Intel designs CPUs for PCs and data centers while trying to build an external foundry business manufacturing chips for other companies. That mix provides exposure to both traditional hardware refreshes and AI infrastructure, but requires heavy investment and disciplined execution. Rakesh outlined four tailwinds that could offset the valuation pressure. First, server manufacturers are reporting accelerating agentic AI demand into 2027. Higher token consumption can require more CPUs alongside GPUs, improving the CPU-to-GPU ratio, while conventional enterprise server refreshes add incremental demand. Second, CPU supply remains constrained. Intel could undership demand through 2027, and major customers may face shortages into next year. Scarcity can support pricing, although it limits how much near-term demand Intel can convert into revenue. Third, Mizuho estimates Intel's advanced-packaging revenue could reach $3.5 billion by 2029, supported by EMIB-T packaging for tensor processing units. External foundry revenue could separately climb to $3.5 billion as Intel's 14A process ramps. Finally, PC demand is exceeding expectations as corporate upgrade cycles emerge. Tight memory supply could stretch the refresh cycle, making the recovery steadier rather than short-lived. For investors, the reduced $92 target captures the tension. Intel has several visible growth levers, but the market may assign lower multiples until foundry execution, supply and AI-driven CPU demand translate into profits. The Neutral rating therefore reflects timing: the opportunity is improving, while confidence in value creation remains incomplete for now. news.Title: Dell’s earning report was bullish for Intel CPU demand, analyst says
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) could reach $200 per share as surging AI workloads drive what Global Equities Research analyst Trip Chowdhry estimates is 16-fold year-over-year growth in CPU demand. Chowdhry published a note arguing that Dell's most recent earnings call provides direct validation of that thesis, pointing to Dell's traditional server revenue rising 122% year-over-year as evidence of accelerating Intel CPU adoption.

Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) is the most direct equity expression of the structural shift Chowdhry describes. The firm's $200 price target and a 2031 EPS estimate of $20 rest on three interlocking arguments: rising CPU-to-GPU ratios in AI clusters, x86's entrenched enterprise position, and the architectural advantages of Intel's Clearwater Forest processor.

Dell's Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke supplied language that Chowdhry seized on. Clarke said on the earnings call that Dell is seeing "demand for new servers that have more cores" and separately described "a growing trend of customers that require meaningful CPU compute capacity to support AI and agentic workflows." Clarke also noted that traditional server revenue "was up 122% as demand remains exceptionally strong." Chowdhry's note states plainly: "This is INTC CPUs."

The demand driver, in Global Equities Research's telling, is a medium-level shift in AI training workloads. "INTC CPUs are seeing 16x y-y growth as Training shifts to Heavy Media - Video, Images and Audio from simple Text," Chowdhry wrote. Processing video, images, and audio is far more compute-intensive than training on text alone, and CPUs are bearing a growing share of that burden alongside GPUs.

The CPU-to-GPU ratio inversion underpins much of the bull case. Two generations ago, Chowdhry notes, one CPU could manage eight GPUs. Today, according to Global Equities Research, it takes two to four CPUs just to keep pace with a single GPU or TPU. That structural change alone implies a multi-fold increase in CPU unit demand per AI server rack, independent of any market-share gains Intel makes against AMD.

On the competitive landscape, Intel's Clearwater Forest leads the core-count comparison that Chowdhry lays out. Clearwater Forest offers 576 cores, versus AMD's Turin Dense at 192 cores and Nvidia's Vera Rubin at 88 cores, which began shipping in August 2026 per Global Equities Research's summary. Chowdhry frames Nvidia's Vera Rubin and Grace products as "GPU Controllers" rather than true CPU competitors, suggesting the two markets are less head-to-head than commonly assumed.

Story Continues

Two additional technical arguments round out the note. First, high-end GPUs are capped at 80 to 192 gigabytes of HBM DRAM memory per unit, whereas Intel x86 servers support terabytes of system DRAM, a meaningful advantage for large language model inference that cannot fit within GPU memory constraints. Second, Intel's AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) instruction set allows x86 CPUs to run INT8, FP16, and BF16 matrix multiplication directly on-chip, enabling real-time inference on midsize LLMs ranging from 7 billion to 13 billion parameters without a discrete GPU or TPU.

Enterprise lock-in adds a defensive moat to the growth story. Global Equities Research notes that over 70% of existing enterprise data centers are built on x86 infrastructure, and that using x86 CPUs eliminates the need to rewrite software, lowering the switching cost for customers who might otherwise consider alternative architectures. That installed base gives Intel a distribution advantage that core-count comparisons alone do not capture.

"We are estimating 2031 INTC EPS to be $20," Chowdhry wrote, though the note does not disclose the P/E multiple or DCF assumptions used to bridge that figure to the $200 price target. Investors assigning their own multiple to the estimate can note that $20 EPS at a 10x multiple would imply $200, though that multiple selection is not attributed to Global Equities Research.

Looking ahead, two near-term catalysts are worth monitoring. Intel's next quarterly earnings report will be the first opportunity to see whether CPU server revenue is tracking toward the growth trajectory that Chowdhry's note implies; any further commentary on Clearwater Forest shipment volumes and data-center order backlogs will either reinforce or challenge the 16x demand thesis. Dell's next earnings call carries similar weight, given that Chowdhry used it as the primary validation event this cycle; a sustained 100%-plus growth rate in traditional server revenue would strengthen the case for Intel CPU market-share gains, while a deceleration would raise questions about whether the demand spike is structural or front-loaded.

news.Title: Intel Witnesses an Uptrend in Estimate Revisions: Is it Worth Buying?
news.Content:
Earnings estimates for Intel Corporation INTC for 2026 and 2027 have moved up 44.12% to $1.47 and 35.42% to $1.95, respectively, over the past 60 days. The positive estimate revisions depict bullish sentiments about the stock's growth potential.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

INTC Rides on Strong AI Traction, Improving Manufacturing Execution

Data Center and AI (DCAI) is emerging as one of Intel's strongest growth engines for the company. DCAI revenue increased 59% year over year to $6.3 billion in the second quarter, supported by strong demand from hyperscale and enterprise customers. Strong server CPU demand and growing adoption of Xeon 6 processors are expected to fuel growth in upcoming quarters.

Intel is rapidly broadening its traditional PC offerings by incorporating AI capabilities. AI PC revenues are up 26% sequentially and represent about two-thirds of segment revenues. At Hot Chips 2026, Intel detailed Wildcat Lake, launched as Intel Core Series 3, for laptops and intelligent edge platforms. Built on Intel 18A, it combines CPU cores, Xe3 graphics with XMX acceleration and an NPU delivering up to 17 TOPS, while marking Intel's first use of UCIe in a processor. Intel has secured 130 Series 3 edge AI design wins, and edge deployments account for 10% of CCPG revenue.

Intel is expanding beyond general-purpose CPUs into customized silicon designed for specific workloads. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, purpose-built silicon revenue increased about 20% sequentially and nearly tripled year over year, reaching an estimated $2 billion run rate, with management targeting $4 billion in the not-too-distant future.

Operational improvements are providing another potential earnings driver. Intel is seeing better yields, faster cycle times and higher factory output across several process nodes. In the second quarter, higher revenue, improved yields and pricing contributed to a non-GAAP gross margin of 41.8%, while operating cash flow reached $7 billion.

Supply Constraints, Stiff Competition, Weak PC Market are Concerns

Intel is dealing with a difficult supply environment even as demand remains strong. Industry-wide shortages of leading-edge wafers, memory and substrates are limiting the company's ability to fully capitalize on the growing customer requirements. Management expects PC consumption to decline at a low-double-digit rate in 2026, citing higher memory prices and supply constraints.

Intel operates in an industry characterized by aggressive competition and rapid technological change. It faces competition from Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Arm Holdings ARM in server CPUs. The broader AI infrastructure market remains highly contested across CPUs, GPUs, ASICs and networking. Intel's confidence in catching up and later leapfrogging competitors depends on timely execution across Clearwater Forest, Diamond Rapids and Coral Rapids.

Intel's global manufacturing and supply chain expose it to geopolitical and trade-related risks. The company specifically highlights tensions involving the United States and China, developments around Taiwan, tariffs and export controls as factors that could disrupt operations.

Story Continues

Price Performance

Intel has gained 271.4% in a year compared with the industry's growth of 35.2%. It has outperformed compared to the Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the S&P 500.

The company has outperformed its peers, AMD and Arm Holdings. AMD has gained 181.6%, while ARM has increased 79.1% during this period.

Key Valuation Metric for Intel

From a valuation standpoint, Intel appears to be relatively cheaper than the industry. Going by the price/book ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 4.48 book value, lower than the industry average of 22.99.

End Note

The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure has created a strong opportunity across Intel's product offerings. In the second quarter, Intel's AI driven business grew more than 70% year over year in the second quarter. The company is expanding its opportunity beyond traditional PCs through AI PCs, edge computing and physical AI applications. This will likely bring long-term benefits. However, supply shortages across wafers, memory and substrates are restricting the company's ability to meet strong customer demand, while aggressive capital spending on manufacturing expansion is weighing on near-term free cash flow. Stiff competition remains a concern. Hence, with a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), Intel appears to be on a middle-of-the-road track, suggesting that investors should exercise caution while trading the stock. news.Title: $1.3 Trillion in Projected Data Center Spending in 2027 Makes These Stocks No-Brainer Buys
news.Content:
Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) released a nugget of information during its Q2 earnings call. It noted that it believes the big five AI hyperscalers will spend around $1.3 trillion in capital expenditures during 2027. That's a simply incredible figure, and it shows there will be much more spending on AI hardware and infrastructure in 2027.

That bodes well for several stocks, but the four I think will benefit most are Nvidia, Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO), Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE: TSM), and Micron (NASDAQ: MU). If you don't own these four, now is the perfect time to scoop up shares, as the growth in 2027 could send these stocks soaring.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Nvidia and Broadcom design the hardware

Both Nvidia and Broadcom are known as fabless design firms, meaning they design the computing units but outsource much of the fabrication to external companies. This makes them a pretty high-margin business, which is great to invest in.

Nvidia makes GPUs, the most widely used accelerated computing units in the AI community. However, some companies are looking for a more specialized approach and turning to Broadcom's design services to build a custom AI chip. The future will be a mix of both computing unit types, not an outright winner. That makes both companies worth considering, and each has some major projections for 2027.

Nvidia believes its revenue will grow at 70% during its next fiscal year, which is amazing, considering it's the world's largest company. Broadcom has long touted 2027 as its breakthrough year and has projected that its AI semiconductor business will cross $100 billion in annual revenue. During Q3 (ending Aug. 2), Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue totaled $16.7 billion, up 221% year over year. There's clearly a ton of growth remaining in this business unit, and if Broadcom delivers on its projection, the stock will be a must-buy.

With the AI hyperscalers likely to ramp up capital expenditures next year, both Broadcom and Nvidia make for genius buys, as they are two of the biggest beneficiaries of this massive spending spree.

Taiwan Semiconductor and Micron make the chips

As mentioned, Nvidia and Broadcom design the chips, but they farm out the work to chip fabrication companies like Taiwan Semiconductor and Micron. These two make different types of chips and are complementary businesses. Taiwan Semiconductor makes logic chips while Micron produces memory chips.

Story Continues

Logic chips are at the heart of computing units like a GPU from Nvidia or a custom AI chip from Broadcom. The design of these chips can make or break a computing unit's performance, and having a top-notch manufacturer with access to the world's most advanced manufacturing technology sets it apart from competitors.

Furthermore, TSMC is the largest logic chip manufacturer by far and the only company in the world with the production capacity to meet massive AI demand. With spending rising, Taiwan Semi is well-positioned to capitalize.

Micron makes memory chips, which are far more commoditized. However, that doesn't mean these chips aren't important. However, the current pace of data center chip demand has left Micron and its peers with insufficient production capacity, and memory chip prices are soaring as a result.

Micron is benefiting from this, and with new memory chip product capacity not expected to be online until mid-2027 and into 2028, the supply crunch could last for some time. Combine that with rising spending expectations, and memory chip prices could be elevated for some time.

That makes Micron a solid stock pick alongside Taiwan Semiconductor, and both should crush the market in 2027.

news.Title: Here Are the First 3 Stocks I'm Buying if the Market Crashes
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) is right around all-time highs right now, and nothing appears to be looming that could send the market lower. However, surprises do pop up and can send the market crashing (or soaring) at a moment's notice. Investors need to have a short list of stocks ready to buy if it goes down tomorrow.

Headlining my list are three stocks: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN). This list could change if the reason for the market sell-off places a specific company right in the crosshairs, but if it's just a general sell-off, I'm buying these three first.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing

The general theme for these three stocks is companies that the world cannot live without. Taiwan Semiconductor is the world's largest chip manufacturer by far, and its chips go into nearly every advanced electronic device. It's also irreplaceable. Taiwan Semiconductor has become the most popular chip foundry for nearly every tech company, and switching away from it is nearly impossible because competitors don't have the capacity that TSMC has.

An investment in Taiwan Semiconductor is a bet that we're going to need more advanced chips in greater quantities, which seems like an extremely safe bet to make. Right now, Taiwan Semiconductor is supplying a lot of chips to the AI build-out, but there are other parts of its business that are unrelated.

Taiwan Semiconductor is one of the safest bets any investor can make in the market, as it's a bet on advanced technology. If the market sells off, Taiwan Semiconductor will be at the top of my list.

Alphabet

Another strongly positioned company is Alphabet. Alphabet operates the Google Search engine, which is an advertising cash cow. While everyone was concerned that AI would replace Google Search, that hasn't happened. Furthermore, Alphabet has integrated AI into Google Search, and it's one of the primary ways the majority of the world interacts with AI on a daily basis.

Another business unit boosted by AI is Alphabet's cloud computing division, Google Cloud. Alphabet has spent hundreds of billions of dollars building out data centers to run AI workloads, and charges by usage. If something causes the market to crash, these workloads won't all of a sudden just stop running. So, Alphabet will receive continuous revenue in good times and bad.

Story Continues

This steady income stream, combined with a dominant platform, makes Alphabet a smart stock to buy and own in any market condition, and it always has a knack for emerging from a downturn stronger than before.

Amazon

Amazon and Alphabet are two similar companies in terms of why I think they're smart buys in a downturn. Amazon has a strong commerce business, and while growth may slow during a downturn, everyone still needs a place to go to buy basic goods. Amazon also has a strong cloud computing platform, Amazon Web Services (AWS), that will stay strong for the exact same reason as Alphabet's.

Similar to Alphabet, Amazon has survived market turbulence before, including the dot-com bubble, the great financial crisis, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Amazon has built a commerce empire and a thriving cloud computing segment that's growing at a rapid rate. I don't think there's anything that will slow Amazon down, and any downturn will be a bump in the road.

Amazon is not only a top stock to buy in a downturn, but I also think it's a strong stock to buy now, as it's benefiting from the strength of AI spending.

林漢偉分析師表示，今日台股回穩反彈，聯準會偏鴿談話讓升息預期降溫，美債殖利率回落，帶動資金重新回流成長股。電子權值股有望反彈，中小型股則觀察記憶體、矽光子與IC設計等主流族群的反彈力道。

news.Title: 4檔記憶體遭狙擊！外資翻臉狂砍9.5萬張 逆勢狂掃「這家面板廠」
news.Content:
台股今（3）日尾盤急殺307點，收在45857點失守46000點大關。外資連兩日狂提款1395億元，其中由「瑤池金母」陳釧瑤操盤的統一台股增長（00981A）遭倒貨近4萬張再度高居賣超榜首，南亞科等4檔記憶體要角也遭變現逾9.5萬張淪苦主；反觀友達獲逆勢掃貨逾5.5萬張，買超榜前十名更有7檔金融股入列，顯示資金正加速轉向防禦型標的。

ABF載板、記憶體淪賣壓震央

台股在電子族群普遍走弱，終場下跌307點，收在45857點，成交值9462億元。三大法人合計賣超637.11億元，其中外資及陸資賣超481.46億元，連兩日賣超1395億元，自營商賣超167.07億元，投信買超11.42億元。

權值股走勢分化，台積電終場微幅上揚5元（或0.2%）至2390 元；聯發科與台達電均上漲 1%；鴻海與台光電則雙雙收黑。

ABF載板族群成為賣壓震央，南電預告第四季BT載板可能凍漲，今日重挫跌停，拖累景碩與欣興雙雙大跌8%、5%；PCB族群同步潰敗，臻鼎-KY重摔8%，金像電與華通也分別下挫 6%及5%；記憶體與被動元件同樣走弱，南亞科與華新科雙雙慘跌 7%，華邦電與國巨也同步暴跌5%。

資金避險大移轉 金融包辦買超 7 席

外資最新買超前十名單中，友達以5.5 萬張奪第一，群創也獲進駐 1.9 萬張，聯電與強茂則分別獲回補2.2萬張及1.6萬張。值得注意的是，金融股強勢包辦7個席次，掃貨遠東銀2.9 萬張，兆豐金與國票金獲買超逾2萬張，合庫金、元大金及第一金買進1.7萬張~1.2萬張不等。顯示資金加速轉向低基期與金融標的進行防禦布局。

反觀外資最新賣超前十名榜單，主要賣壓集中於記憶體族群與主動ETF和高息ETF。其中，主動型ETF 00981A（主動統一台股增長）慘遭外資拋售3.8萬張，高居賣超榜首；記憶體族群的南亞科遭砍3.4 萬張、華邦電2.6 萬張、力積電1.8 萬張、旺宏也被出脫1.5 萬張，4檔合計變現逾9.5萬張；此外，高股息ETF 同樣遭減碼，00918、00919、00929遭賣超1.6萬張~1萬張不等。

法人分析，美伊局勢變數多增溫通膨疑慮，加上國際油價走揚與美債殖利率居高不下，加深市場升息預期，短期將對科技股高估值形成壓力，促使外資在台股期現貨布局轉趨謹慎。

news.Title: 外資賣超481億！ 南亞科、華邦電遭砍翻 「這檔」爆買5.5萬張

外資買超友達、金融股

外資今日買超集中在友達（2409），單日買超5萬5437張，居買超第一名；遠東銀（2845）買超2萬9742張，排名第二。金融股表現最為集中，兆豐金（2886）買超2萬3261張、國票金（2889）買超2萬412張，此外合庫金（5880）、元大金（2885）及第一金（2892）分別獲買超1萬7430張、1萬7375張及1萬2524張。電子股則以聯電（2303）買超2萬2021張最多，群創（3481）買超1萬9021張，強茂（2481）也獲買超1萬6999張。

記憶體遭外資大砍

賣超方面，主動統一台股增長（00981A）遭外資賣超3萬8014張，成為今日賣超冠軍。記憶體族群則出現明顯調節，南亞科（2408）遭賣超3萬4399張，華邦電（2344）賣超2萬6737張，力積電（6770）賣超1萬8954張，旺宏（2337）也遭賣超1萬5138張。此外，臺企銀（2834）遭賣超2萬3184張，位居個股賣超第四名。

ETF同樣出現大額賣超，大華優利高填息30（00918）遭賣超1萬6734張，群益台灣精選高息（00919）賣超1萬4242張，主動凱基台灣（00407A）賣超1萬1544張，復華台灣科技優息（00929）則賣超1萬704張。從今日籌碼來看，外資操作呈現明顯的「買金融、賣電子」格局，尤其記憶體族群遭集中調節，成為盤面焦點。

記憶體「蛋雕」網熱議

外資買超名單幾乎被金融股包辦，也引發PTT網友討論，有人直呼「金金有味」、「好多黃色的金銀」、「金融最後一棒不要不信」，甚至笑稱外資是不是「要把銀行買下來」。另一方面，南亞科、華邦電等記憶體股遭大砍，也讓網友留言「華邦牙科天天倒不完」、「電子蛋雕」、「原來是記憶體洗產地被檢調搜索啊」、「記憶體、載板、被動，三大漲價題材OVER」。

news.Title: 【Follow法人】記憶體又成提款機？外資砍南亞科華邦電逾6萬張 反手買台積電235億元
news.Content:
（下午4點50分更新買賣超個股）

台股今（3）日震盪走低，終場下跌307點，失守4萬6千點關卡。三大法人合計賣超637.11億元，其中外資今日再賣超481.45億元，呈現連2賣，兩日累計提款1,394.99億元。資深台股分析師蔡明翰表示，外資近期賣超主要反映台股位階相對偏高，法人目前仍處於觀望、多空分歧階段。觀察個股，記憶體再成提款重災區，南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）合計遭砍逾6萬張；台積電（2330）則逆勢獲外資加碼235億元。

外資今日賣超前三大：00981A、南亞科、華邦電

外資今日賣超以主動統一台股增長（00981A）居冠，單日遭調節逾3.8萬張；記憶體股南亞科（2408）遭外資砍逾3.4萬張排名第二；華邦電（2344）則遭賣超逾2.6萬張，位居第三。

值得注意的是，記憶體族群成為外資今日主要提款對象，除了南亞科、華邦電包辦第二、三名外，力積電（6770）、旺宏（2337）也分別遭賣超約1.9萬張及1.5萬張，前十大賣超榜中共有4檔記憶體相關個股入列。

ETF同樣遭到外資調節，除了賣超冠軍主動統一台股增長外，大華優利高填息30（00918）、群益台灣精選高息（00919）、主動凱基台灣（00407A）及復華台灣科技優息（00929）也擠進前十大，前十大賣超榜共有5檔ETF入列。

外資今日買超前三大：友達、遠東銀、兆豐金

觀察外資今日買超個股，面板股友達（2409）以買超逾5.5萬張高居第一，遠東銀（2845）獲外資買超近3萬張排名第二，兆豐金（2886）則獲加碼逾2.3萬張，位居第三。

外資今日買盤也明顯集中金融股，除了遠東銀、兆豐金外，國票金（2889）、合庫金（5880）、元大金（2885）及第一金（2892）也進入前十大，前十大買超個股中共有6檔金融股。

其餘個股方面，晶圓代工廠聯電（2303）獲外資買超逾2.2萬張；另一檔面板股群創（3481）也獲加碼逾1.9萬張。值得注意的是台積電（2330）也獲外資買超9,838張，若以今日收盤價估算，外資單日加碼金額約235億元。

外資連2賣是轉空？蔡明翰：高檔正常調節

蔡明翰指出，台股前波一度逼近4萬7千點，準備挑戰歷史高點，相較之下，與台股連動度較高的費城半導體指數及韓股仍處整理階段，台股位階明顯較高，因此外資近期出現獲利調節並不意外，他認為，目前整體格局仍是在消化上半年大漲後的漲幅，趨勢尚未出現明顯改變。

至於外資何時可能重新轉為連續買超？蔡明翰認為，關鍵仍要觀察美國科技股，以費城半導體指數為主，若費半重新站回月線、趨勢逐步轉強，資金重新回流科技及AI族群，屆時才較有機會看到外資轉為較具連續性的買超，台股也才有進一步向上挑戰的空間。

蔡明翰指出，目前法人並非明顯偏多或偏空，而是處於觀望階段，後續仍須等待美國科技股轉強，才有機會看到法人資金出現較具持續性的回流。

外資再砍481億元 三大法人合計賣超637億元

根據證交所公布籌碼動向，三大法人今日合計賣超637.11億元。其中，外資今日再砍481.45億元，呈連2賣，累計賣超1,394.99億元。

其中投信則是逆勢買超，投信今日由賣轉買，合計買超11.41億元。自營商則持續賣超167.06億元，其中自行買賣買超56.78億元，避險操作賣超110.28億元。

台股今日震盪走低，加權指數終場收在45,857點，下跌307點，失守4萬6千點關卡。成交金額約9,892億元；權王台積電（2330）終場收在2,390元，上漲5元。

news.Content:

news.Content:
小編今天（3）日精選5件國內外重要財經大事。摩根士丹利證券參加SEMICON Taiwan指出，記憶體產業的價值創造正從過去單純追求位元微縮，逐步轉向架構層級的創新，在AI發展加速環境中，記憶體正逐漸成為系統層級的關鍵差異化因素，看好愛普*（6531）、旺宏（2337）前景，均給予「優於大盤」投資評等，推測合理股價1,666元與220元。

摩根士丹利證券指出，在目前2.5D架構之後，3D堆疊很可能成為未來的主要發展趨勢。三星的zHBM與更廣泛的DRAM-on-Logic概念，皆顯示記憶體正從配置在運算晶片旁，逐步走向與晶片垂直整合的架構，如此一來，混合鍵合、WoW整合與散熱共同設計重要性都將進一步提升；大摩看好，愛普*有望成為新興3D WoW堆疊商機的潛在受惠者。

【2】南亞科8月營收再攀新高

DRAM景氣持續火熱，南亞科（2408）2日公布2026年8月自結合併營收446.9億元，月增1.88％、年增560.85％，再創單月歷史新高；累計今年前八月營收2,201.94億元，較去年同期大增638.19％，營運動能持續升溫。

【3】利空夾擊 外資砍台股913億

萬寶投顧總監蔡明彰表示，目前全球主要經濟體公債殖利率飆升，公債殖利率風暴為9月最大黑天鵝。其中，美10年公債殖利率若再往5％靠攏且費半指數失守半年線，台股不排除面臨補跌壓力。

G20（20國集團）創新部長級會議1日於北卡羅來納州登場，來自世界各地的官員與科技業高層齊聚一堂，討論AI革命帶來的顛覆與機會。億萬富豪馬斯克在會中表示，AI可能會讓全球經濟規模增加20％～30％，未來十年內人形機器人數量至少達10億台。

美國與伊朗1日爆發7月以來最激烈交火，美軍對伊朗多個目標發動空襲，伊朗隨即攻擊美軍數座中東基地，消息帶動國際油價躥揚，布蘭特原油一度升破97美元，市場擔憂衝突升溫恐讓油價突破100美元大關。中東動盪拖累全球股市軟腳，日韓股市跌勢尤其明顯，日股狂瀉近1,900點，韓股重挫4％。

news.Title: Zacks Industry Outlook Highlights MACOM Technology, Monolithic Power and Semtech
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – September 2, 2026 – Today, Zacks Equity Research discusses MACOM Technology MTSI, Monolithic Power MPWR and Semtech Corp. SMTC.

Industry: Analog Mixed-Signal Semiconductors

Link: https://www.zacks.com/commentary/2983350/buy-analog-mixed-signal-players-macom-monolithic-semtech

The analog/mixed-signal semiconductor market is poised for solid growth this year, following a strong 2025. Macro and geopolitical developments remain overhangs, with capacity constraints in certain mature and specialty processes increasingly tightening supply and supporting prices.

We expect that these concerns will be overridden by the cyclical recovery in semiconductors coupled with strong end market demand from AI, industrial automation and automotive. We think there may be significant opportunities here and our bets are particularly on MACOM Technology , Monolithic Power and Semtech Corp. .

2026 growth data from World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) – provided in Spring 2026 – projects 90% growth in semiconductors this year, mainly driven by memory, which is expected to grow around 250%. The analog segment is expected to grow a relatively sedate 10% because of its greater exposure to the industrial and auto markets. However, the recovery in these markets, along with AI-related demand, is providing additional support.

While valuations appear rich compared to the broader tech sector as well as the S&P benchmark, risk appears limited given the significant growth levers that could support multi-year expansion.

About the Industry

The electronic gadgets we use to accurately read our commands, and record, store, retrieve and process the information we throw at them run on semiconductor technology, whether analog (enabling the recording and measurement of real-world information), digital (processing information available in machine-readable language) or mixed signal (enabling conversion of analog signals to digital or digital to analog among other things). Most electronic gadgets use a combination of these components, whether in consumer, industrial, auto, medical, communications, or IoT and other markets.

The industry is cyclical and prices are elastic. Players usually serve multiple markets that offset their individual seasonality, or focus on certain core markets for which they have highly differentiated technology and relationships.

Growth Prospects Strong Despite Macro and Geopolitics

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and data-center infrastructure has emerged as an increasingly important growth driver for the analog and mixed-signal semiconductor industry. AI computing is increasing demand not only for GPUs and memory but also for the supporting semiconductor infrastructure required to power, connect and control increasingly dense computing systems. AI data centers require sophisticated power-management and power-delivery solutions, high-speed signal conditioning, optical and electrical connectivity, timing components and thermal-management technologies. As AI clusters scale, rising power consumption and increasing data-transfer speeds are driving greater semiconductor content per system, creating significant opportunities for suppliers of analog, mixed-signal, power and high-speed connectivity products.

Analog and mixed-signal semiconductor demand continues to be driven by several powerful and interconnected secular trends . Foremost among them is the rapid electrification of transportation, particularly the rise of electric vehicles , which significantly increases demand for analog components such as power management ICs, battery monitoring systems and sensor interfaces. Closely related is the expansion of IoT and edge devices , where billions of connected nodes rely on mixed-signal chips with ultra-low power consumption. Industrial automation is another major driver, as smart factories and Industry 4.0 applications depend heavily on precise sensing, control systems and predictive maintenance enabled by these technologies. In parallel, the rollout of 5G and advanced connectivity infrastructure is fueling demand for high-performance RF components, data converters and timing solutions that rely on mixed-signal integration. Additionally, the global energy transition is accelerating the need for advanced power management systems in renewable energy, EV charging and smart grid applications, making power analog the largest segment in the market. While consumer electronics continue to contribute, their growth has matured, shifting focus from volume expansion to increased functionality per device, which still raises analog content. While elevated memory prices are likely to pressure consumer electronics and other memory-intensive applications, AI infrastructure spending is increasingly offsetting this weakness. Consequently, the outlook for analog and mixed-signal semiconductors is becoming increasingly differentiated by end market rather than being uniformly cyclical.

In general, semiconductor pricing is robust when capacity is tight and utilization high. Companies start adding capacity when they anticipate the next big growth cycle which usually continues for several years. AI is a major driver of the current build cycle and AI demand is expected to remain strong for years to come, lengthening the cycle and supporting prices. Supply chain efficiency also has an effect on chip prices. The significant increase in chip demand is driven by AI, data centers, IoT and EVs and strategic imperatives for countries in the race to technological superiority. However, capacity constraints are becoming increasingly evident in certain mature and specialty processes, including 200mm manufacturing platforms commonly used for analog, power and other mature-node semiconductor products. AI-related demand is competing for some of the same manufacturing resources, and foundries are also reallocating capacity toward higher-margin products. Therefore, pricing should remain relatively resilient in the foreseeable future, particularly for differentiated products and those facing capacity constraints.

The push toward greater system integration and application-specific solutions is significantly reshaping the analog/mixed-signal industry. The need to reduce system cost, power consumption and physical footprint is driving companies to integrate analog, digital, sensing, processing and connectivity functions into highly integrated solutions. This shift is being enabled by advanced process technologies like CMOS scaling and specialized nodes (for example SOI and BiCMOS). This raises the technical complexity of design, especially in noise isolation, signal integrity and mixed-signal verification, increasing development time and demand for specialized analog design talent. It can also increase the value per chip, as customers pay more for integrated solutionsthat reduce system complexity and development costs. Leading analog and mixed-signal companies like TXN, ADI, Infineon, STM and NXP are increasingly developing highly integrated, application-specific solutions, particularly in automotive, industrial and communications markets.

Story Continues

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Strong Growth Prospects

The Zacks Semiconductor – Analog and Mixed industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank of #23, which places it in the top 9% of the nearly 250 Zacks-classified industries. The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates improving near-term prospects.

Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. The industry's positioning in the top 50% of Zacks-ranked industries is based on the earnings outlook of the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions over the past year, we see that 2026 estimates have been rising more or less steadily over the past year, though more significantly so in the last four months.

For 2027 as well, the more significant increases have come in the last four months. Overall, the 2026 estimate has increased 34.6% over the past year, while the 2027 estimate has increased 32.5%.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let's take a look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture.

Stock Market Performance Shows Solid Returns

The Semiconductor – Analog and Mixed industry currently trades at a premium to both the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the S&P 500.

Overall, the industry has gained 37.4% over the past year while the broader sector gained 29.9% and the S&P 500 gained 20.8%.

Industry's Current Valuation a Premium

On the basis of forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, the industry is trading at a 23.22X multiple, which is a 17.5% discount to its median value over the past year. It is however a 12.4% premium to the broader market's 20.65X as well as a 15.5% premium to the S&P 500's 20.1X.

The industry has traded between the 23.22X and 36.39X multiples over the past year.

3 Stocks Worth Buying

Despite growing macro uncertainty, a cyclical recovery and strong industrial and AI demand are serving as powerful tailwinds for the industry. The following stocks are worth a closer look:

MACOM Technology Solutions : Headquartered in Lowell, Massachusetts, MACOM designs and manufactures high-performance semiconductor products for the data center, telecommunications, and industrial and defense markets. MACOM's semiconductor solutions are used across high-speed optical networking, wireless infrastructure, radar, aerospace and defense, and high-performance computing applications.

The company is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure demand, an expanding optical connectivity portfolio and emerging opportunities in satellite communications. A key growth driver is the rapid buildout of AI data centers, which require increasingly high-speed, low-latency connections between processors, switches and other components. MACOM supplies critical optical and analog components used in these connectivity systems, positioning it as an important semiconductor supplier to AI networking infrastructure. The company is expanding its exposure to higher-speed optical technologies, with solutions supporting 800G and 1.6T connectivity and emerging 3.2T architectures.

MACOM is also expanding its opportunity in satellite communications, particularly as low-Earth orbit (LEO) networks drive demand for higher-frequency and higher-bandwidth connectivity. Its RF and optical solutions support satellite communications, providing an additional growth opportunity beyond traditional telecommunications and data centers.

That said, MACOM's growth is increasingly tied to the AI data-center investment cycle, creating exposure to a potentially cyclical and concentrated market. Its dependence on hyperscalers could amplify this risk, as delays or reductions in customer capital spending could materially affect demand. Competition in optical connectivity could pressure pricing and margins as higher-speed technologies become more standardized. The company also faces execution risks as it ramps 1.6T and 3.2T products, particularly as competition intensifies in next-generation optical connectivity. Meanwhile, satellite communications remains an emerging opportunity and is not yet a significant contributor to revenue.

MACOM's third quarter earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.5%. The estimates for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 (ending September) are up 45 cents (9.1%) and $1.49 (22.7%), respectively, in the last 30 days. This represents revenue and earnings growth of a respective 36.8% and 55% in 2026 and 35.8% and 49.7% in 2027.

Shares of this Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) company have appreciated 105.8% in the past year.

Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. : Headquartered in Kirkland, Washington, Monolithic is a fabless semiconductor company that develops high-performance power-management and power-conversion solutions. The company serves a diversified range of markets, including storage and computing, enterprise data, automotive, communications, consumer and industrial applications.

MPWR is increasingly positioned to benefit from the rapid rise in power requirements across AI infrastructure and other high-performance computing applications, with recent results indicating a significant acceleration in demand. Total revenue increased 47.6% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, highlighting the strength of the company's overall growth trajectory. Enterprise Data revenue surged 164.3% year over year in the quarter, on the back of 97.7% growth in quarter one, after declining 2% in 2025.

The sharp rebound reflects accelerating demand for AI and server power-management solutions, positioning Enterprise Data as an increasingly important growth driver for the company. As AI servers require increasingly dense and efficient power delivery, the company stands to benefit from rising power content per system as it develops more compact, high-power and efficient solutions, advanced packaging technologies and next-generation architectures such as 800V data-center power.

Importantly, growth extends beyond AI: communications revenue was up 78.3% in the quarter, while automotive and industrial increased 8.2% and 17.3%, respectively. In 2025, automotive revenue grew 43.1%, communications 36.8%, storage and computing 46.0% and industrial 35.3%. This diversification implies multiple secular growth avenues while reducing reliance on any single market. Its increasingly integrated power solutions and modules can further increase content per system across served markets, strengthening customer relationships and supporting the company's long-term growth opportunity.

Given the recent growth trajectory, expectations for AI-driven growth have risen sharply, increasing the risk of disappointment if data-center capital spending slows or is delayed. Sustaining triple-digit Enterprise Data growth will also become more difficult as the base expands, while customer concentration and dependence on large hyperscalers could make revenue growth more volatile if customers alter their spending plans.

The company faces additional execution risks as it ramps next-generation architectures such as 800V data-center power. Competition remains intense, while a premium valuation leaves limited room for execution shortfalls and could result in significant multiple compression if AI growth moderates.

Monolithic Power's second quarter earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.5%. The estimates for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 (ending December) are up $2.93 (12.1%) and $4.88 (16.3%), respectively, in the last 30 days. This works out to expected revenue and earnings growth of 46.4% and 52.6% in 2026 and 26.3% and 28.1% in 2027.

Shares of the Zacks Rank #1 company have appreciated 51.7% in the past year.

Semtech Corporation : Camarillo, California-based Semtech is a semiconductor and connectivity company providing high-performance solutions for data centers, communications infrastructure, industrial applications and IoT. Its portfolio spans high-speed signal-integrity products for optical and copper data communications, analog and mixed-signal solutions, and wireless connectivity technologies including LoRa®. The company also provides IoT modules, gateways and connectivity solutions supporting cellular and other wireless networks.

Semtech is benefiting from improving demand across its data-center, industrial and IoT businesses, with recent results showing accelerating growth and expanding margins. Data-center revenue increased 91% year over year in the latest quarter, outpacing 33% growth in total company revenue, as AI-driven increases in bandwidth and connectivity requirements support demand for its optical and connectivity products. FiberEdge and CopperEdge products position the company to benefit from rising bandwidth requirements, as increasingly demanding applications drive higher component content per system.

Beyond data centers, LoRa-enabled solutions are supporting growth in industrial and IoT applications by providing low-power, long-range connectivity for connected devices and infrastructure. The improving growth profile is translating into stronger operating leverage, with Q2 FY2027 adjusted operating margin expanding to 24.4% from 18.8% a year earlier.

The combination of accelerating data-center demand, expanding content per system, growing IoT adoption and strong margin expansion provides a solid foundation for sustained earnings growth.The stock increasingly reflects the AI/data-center opportunity but must execute successfully on a rapid transition toward higher-speed optical connectivity. At the same time, it remains meaningfully exposed to cyclical markets. If AI spending slows, the company's other businesses may not be strong enough to offset weaker data-center demand, leaving the shares vulnerable to a pullback.

Semtech topped earnings estimates in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (ending January). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2027 is up 67 cents (25.2%) in the last seven days with the 2027 estimate jumping $1.56 (42.7%) in the same period. Revenue and earnings are expected to increase a respective 41.5% and 94.7% in 2027 and a respective 27.5% and 56.5% the following year.

The electronic gadgets we use to accurately read our commands, and record, store, retrieve and process the information we throw at them run on semiconductor technology, whether analog (enabling the recording and measurement of real-world information), digital (processing information available in machine-readable language) or mixed signal (enabling conversion of analog signals to digital or digital to analog among other things). Most electronic gadgets use a combination of these components, whether in consumer, industrial, auto, medical, communications, or IoT and other markets.

The industry is cyclical and prices are elastic. Players usually serve multiple markets that offset their individual seasonality, or focus on certain core markets for which they have highly differentiated technology and relationships.

Growth Prospects Strong Despite Macro and Geopolitics

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and data-center infrastructure has emerged as an increasingly important growth driver for the analog and mixed-signal semiconductor industry. AI computing is increasing demand not only for GPUs and memory but also for the supporting semiconductor infrastructure required to power, connect and control increasingly dense computing systems. AI data centers require sophisticated power-management and power-delivery solutions, high-speed signal conditioning, optical and electrical connectivity, timing components and thermal-management technologies. As AI clusters scale, rising power consumption and increasing data-transfer speeds are driving greater semiconductor content per system, creating significant opportunities for suppliers of analog, mixed-signal, power and high-speed connectivity products.

Story Continues

Analog and mixed-signal semiconductor demand continues to be driven by several powerful and interconnected secular trends . Foremost among them is the rapid electrification of transportation, particularly the rise of electric vehicles , which significantly increases demand for analog components such as power management ICs, battery monitoring systems and sensor interfaces. Closely related is the expansion of IoT and edge devices , where billions of connected nodes rely on mixed-signal chips with ultra-low power consumption. Industrial automation is another major driver, as smart factories and Industry 4.0 applications depend heavily on precise sensing, control systems and predictive maintenance enabled by these technologies. In parallel, the rollout of 5G and advanced connectivity infrastructure is fueling demand for high-performance RF components, data converters and timing solutions that rely on mixed-signal integration. Additionally, the global energy transition is accelerating the need for advanced power management systems in renewable energy, EV charging and smart grid applications, making power analog the largest segment in the market. While consumer electronics continue to contribute, their growth has matured, shifting focus from volume expansion to increased functionality per device, which still raises analog content. While elevated memory prices are likely to pressure consumer electronics and other memory-intensive applications, AI infrastructure spending is increasingly offsetting this weakness. Consequently, the outlook for analog and mixed-signal semiconductors is becoming increasingly differentiated by end market rather than being uniformly cyclical.

In general, semiconductor pricing is robust when capacity is tight and utilization high. Companies start adding capacity when they anticipate the next big growth cycle which usually continues for several years. AI is a major driver of the current build cycle and AI demand is expected to remain strong for years to come, lengthening the cycle and supporting prices. Supply chain efficiency also has an effect on chip prices. The significant increase in chip demand is driven by AI, data centers, IoT and EVs and strategic imperatives for countries in the race to technological superiority. However, capacity constraints are becoming increasingly evident in certain mature and specialty processes, including 200mm manufacturing platforms commonly used for analog, power and other mature-node semiconductor products. AI-related demand is competing for some of the same manufacturing resources, and foundries are also reallocating capacity toward higher-margin products. Therefore, pricing should remain relatively resilient in the foreseeable future, particularly for differentiated products and those facing capacity constraints.

The push toward greater system integration and application-specific solutions is significantly reshaping the analog/mixed-signal industry. The need to reduce system cost, power consumption and physical footprint is driving companies to integrate analog, digital, sensing, processing and connectivity functions into highly integrated solutions. This shift is being enabled by advanced process technologies like CMOS scaling and specialized nodes (for example SOI and BiCMOS). This raises the technical complexity of design, especially in noise isolation, signal integrity and mixed-signal verification, increasing development time and demand for specialized analog design talent. It can also increase the value per chip, as customers pay more for integrated solutionsthat reduce system complexity and development costs. Leading analog and mixed-signal companies like TXN, ADI, Infineon, STM and NXP are increasingly developing highly integrated, application-specific solutions, particularly in automotive, industrial and communications markets.

Zacks Industry Rank Indicates Strong Growth Prospects

The Zacks Semiconductor – Analog and Mixed industry is housed within the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector. It carries a Zacks Industry Rank of #23, which places it in the top 9% of the nearly 250 Zacks-classified industries. The group's Zacks Industry Rank, which is basically the average of the Zacks Rank of all the member stocks, indicates improving near-term prospects.

Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1. The industry's positioning in the top 50% of Zacks-ranked industries is based on the earnings outlook of the constituent companies in aggregate. Looking at the aggregate earnings estimate revisions over the past year, we see that 2026 estimates have been rising more or less steadily over the past year, though more significantly so in the last four months.

For 2027 as well, the more significant increases have come in the last four months. Overall, the 2026 estimate has increased 34.6% over the past year, while the 2027 estimate has increased 32.5%.

Before we present a few stocks that you may want to consider for your portfolio, let's take a look at the industry's recent stock-market performance and valuation picture.

Stock Market Performance Shows Solid Returns

The Semiconductor – Analog and Mixed industry currently trades at a premium to both the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the S&P 500.

Overall, the industry has gained 37.4% over the past year while the broader sector gained 29.9% and the S&P 500 gained 20.8%.

Industry's Current Valuation a Premium

On the basis of forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, the industry is trading at a 23.22X multiple, which is a 17.5% discount to its median value over the past year. It is however a 12.4% premium to the broader market's 20.65X as well as a 15.5% premium to the S&P 500's 20.1X.

3 Stocks Worth Buying

Despite growing macro uncertainty, a cyclical recovery and strong industrial and AI demand are serving as powerful tailwinds for the industry. The following stocks are worth a closer look:

MACOM Technology Solutions (MTSI) : Headquartered in Lowell, Massachusetts, MACOM designs and manufactures high-performance semiconductor products for the data center, telecommunications, and industrial and defense markets. MACOM's semiconductor solutions are used across high-speed optical networking, wireless infrastructure, radar, aerospace and defense, and high-performance computing applications.

The company is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure demand, an expanding optical connectivity portfolio and emerging opportunities in satellite communications. A key growth driver is the rapid buildout of AI data centers, which require increasingly high-speed, low-latency connections between processors, switches and other components. MACOM supplies critical optical and analog components used in these connectivity systems, positioning it as an important semiconductor supplier to AI networking infrastructure. The company is expanding its exposure to higher-speed optical technologies, with solutions supporting 800G and 1.6T connectivity and emerging 3.2T architectures.

MACOM is also expanding its opportunity in satellite communications, particularly as low-Earth orbit (LEO) networks drive demand for higher-frequency and higher-bandwidth connectivity. Its RF and optical solutions support satellite communications, providing an additional growth opportunity beyond traditional telecommunications and data centers.

That said, MACOM's growth is increasingly tied to the AI data-center investment cycle, creating exposure to a potentially cyclical and concentrated market. Its dependence on hyperscalers could amplify this risk, as delays or reductions in customer capital spending could materially affect demand. Competition in optical connectivity could pressure pricing and margins as higher-speed technologies become more standardized. The company also faces execution risks as it ramps 1.6T and 3.2T products, particularly as competition intensifies in next-generation optical connectivity. Meanwhile, satellite communications remains an emerging opportunity and is not yet a significant contributor to revenue.

MACOM's third quarter earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.5%. The estimates for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 (ending September) are up 45 cents (9.1%) and $1.49 (22.7%), respectively, in the last 30 days. Monolithic Power Systems, Inc. (MPWR) : Headquartered in Kirkland, Washington, Monolithic is a fabless semiconductor company that develops high-performance power-management and power-conversion solutions. The company serves a diversified range of markets, including storage and computing, enterprise data, automotive, communications, consumer and industrial applications.

MPWR is increasingly positioned to benefit from the rapid rise in power requirements across AI infrastructure and other high-performance computing applications, with recent results indicating a significant acceleration in demand. Enterprise Data revenue surged 164.3% year over year in the quarter, on the back of 97.7% growth in quarter one, after declining 2% in 2025.

The sharp rebound reflects accelerating demand for AI and server power-management solutions, positioning Enterprise Data as an increasingly important growth driver for the company. As AI servers require increasingly dense and efficient power delivery, the company stands to benefit from rising power content per system as it develops more compact, high-power and efficient solutions, advanced packaging technologies and next-generation architectures such as 800V data-center power.

Importantly, growth extends beyond AI: communications revenue was up 78.3% in the quarter, while automotive and industrial increased 8.2% and 17.3%, respectively. In 2025, automotive revenue grew 43.1%, communications 36.8%, storage and computing 46.0% and industrial 35.3%. This diversification implies multiple secular growth avenues while reducing reliance on any single market. Its increasingly integrated power solutions and modules can further increase content per system across served markets, strengthening customer relationships and supporting the company's long-term growth opportunity.

Given the recent growth trajectory, expectations for AI-driven growth have risen sharply, increasing the risk of disappointment if data-center capital spending slows or is delayed. Sustaining triple-digit Enterprise Data growth will also become more difficult as the base expands, while customer concentration and dependence on large hyperscalers could make revenue growth more volatile if customers alter their spending plans.

The company faces additional execution risks as it ramps next-generation architectures such as 800V data-center power. Competition remains intense, while a premium valuation leaves limited room for execution shortfalls and could result in significant multiple compression if AI growth moderates.

Monolithic Power's second quarter earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 10.5%. This works out to expected revenue and earnings growth of 46.4% and 52.6% in 2026 and 26.3% and 28.1% in 2027.

Shares of the Zacks Rank #1 company have appreciated 51.7% in the past year.

Semtech Corporation (SMTC) : Camarillo, California-based Semtech is a semiconductor and connectivity company providing high-performance solutions for data centers, communications infrastructure, industrial applications and IoT. Its portfolio spans high-speed signal-integrity products for optical and copper data communications, analog and mixed-signal solutions, and wireless connectivity technologies including LoRa®. The company also provides IoT modules, gateways and connectivity solutions supporting cellular and other wireless networks.

Semtech is benefiting from improving demand across its data-center, industrial and IoT businesses, with recent results showing accelerating growth and expanding margins. Data-center revenue increased 91% year over year in the latest quarter, outpacing 33% growth in total company revenue, as AI-driven increases in bandwidth and connectivity requirements support demand for its optical and connectivity products. FiberEdge and CopperEdge products position the company to benefit from rising bandwidth requirements, as increasingly demanding applications drive higher component content per system.

Beyond data centers, LoRa-enabled solutions are supporting growth in industrial and IoT applications by providing low-power, long-range connectivity for connected devices and infrastructure. The improving growth profile is translating into stronger operating leverage, with Q2 FY2027 adjusted operating margin expanding to 24.4% from 18.8% a year earlier.

The combination of accelerating data-center demand, expanding content per system, growing IoT adoption and strong margin expansion provides a solid foundation for sustained earnings growth.The stock increasingly reflects the AI/data-center opportunity but must execute successfully on a rapid transition toward higher-speed optical connectivity. At the same time, it remains meaningfully exposed to cyclical markets. If AI spending slows, the company's other businesses may not be strong enough to offset weaker data-center demand, leaving the shares vulnerable to a pullback.

news.Title: Forget the Biggest Chip Stocks — Analysts Say Buy These 2 Names
news.Content:
Chips are big business and make big headlines.

Globally, according to Fortune Business Insights, the semiconductor market was valued at $598.06 billion in 2025, and is expected to reach more than $1.47 trillion by 2034, representing a CAGR of 10.60% over the period.

The US holds a vital position in the chip industry. The American market, with its combination of design and innovation leadership in semiconductors, its advanced manufacturing capabilities, and its strong protections for intellectual property, is a natural host for strong chip companies and a high level of industry talent. And that makes American chip companies a natural target for investors. Nvidia, the world's largest chipmaker, is also the largest firm on Wall Street, with a market cap in excess of $5.2 trillion.

Promotion

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

However, two of Wall Street's top-ranked analysts are saying that investors should look past the multi-trillion-dollar industry giants, and even look past the multi-hundred-billion-dollar rising stars – because there are small names worth buying. These are chip makers with double-digit-billion-dollar market cap values – but with potential to bring solid upside to the table.

We've opened up the database at TipRanks to get a good look at two names which are getting love from some 5-star analysts. Here's a closer look at them, to see just what's making them compelling choices today.

Lattice Semiconductor Corporation ( LSCC )

First up on this list is Lattice Semiconductor, a firm that has built itself a sound niche in the industry by focusing on a specific role, mastering it, and riding it to consistent profitability. For Lattice, that role is in the design, production, and distribution of low-power and power-efficient field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). The company has over 40 years' experience, working at the leading edge of the semiconductor field, and has become the industry's leader in the supply of FPGAs.

These chips are used in a variety of applications, including control, secure connectivity, and power management in smart computing, mobile devices, industrial and automotive systems. FPGAs are also widely used in data centers; Lattice doesn't provide the headline-grabbing GPUs and CPUs, but its chips are used alongside these chips to handle power sequencing and protocol bridging. In addition, as data centers expand and their architecture evolves, Lattice is finding that demand for its products is also expanding.

Story Continues

In an important recent move, on the subject of expansion, in July, Lattice completed its acquisition of AMI, a provider of platform firmware and infrastructure manageability technology for cloud and AI. The combination of Lattice with AMI will meet the hardware and firmware needs of major hyperscalers, original equipment manufacturers, and neocloud providers. The transaction was valued at $1.65 billion, with $1 billion of that in cash, and $650 million conducted in stock.

Turning to Lattice's most recent financial results, made public in the 2Q26 release earlier this month, we find that the company's quarterly revenue was a company record, at $201.1 million. That top line was up just over 62% year-over-year, and beat the forecast by $15.5 million. At the bottom line, the company realized a non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, a figure that was up 12 cents per share from the prior quarter and was 8 cents per share better than had been anticipated. The non-GAAP free cash flow in Q2 came to $81.3 million.

While Lattice's market cap of $16.2 billion is hardly more than a footnote compared to the industry's mega-cap leaders, it still puts the company solidly in the large-cap category – and the shares are up some 57% for 2026.

The stock has caught the eye of Benchmark analyst Gary Mobley, a 5-star expert on the chip field, who explains his upbeat view of the company, saying, "We see Lattice as a significant share gainer in the programmable logic IC market, driven by: 1) Lattice expanding into the mid-size field programmable gate array (FPGA) market; and 2) strong market positioning in data center compute and networking, which benefits from the current AI spend cycle. We also see a margin improvement story driven by: 1) a greater mix of Lattice FPGAs shipping with system-level software; 2) the recent acquisition of AMI; 3) more revenue scale; and 4) pricing power."

Looking forward, Mobley, who ranks among the top 4% of Street stock experts, goes on to say of the chip-maker, "Our bullish investment thesis for Lattice is mostly growth oriented. However, the growth for Lattice does not necessarily come from growth in the overall FPGA market, although we are forecasting LDD-% compound annual growth (CAGR) for the programmable logic device market from 2024 to 2028. Rather, the growth for Lattice comes from: 1) FPGAs becoming a more viable alternative to more costly, less flexible application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) and application specific standard product (ASSP) alternatives; and 2) Lattice capturing more market share in the low-and mid-tier portion of the FPGA market, as larger rivals lose focus on this segment."

When he puts all of this together, Mobley comes to a solid 'Buy' recommendation for LSCC shares, which he backs up with a $160 price target. Mobley's price target indicates that the stock has room for a 39% upside potential in the coming year. (To watch Mobley's track record, click here .)

Of the 11 recent analyst recommendations on Lattice, 10 are Buys and 1 is a Sell, giving the stock its Strong Buy consensus rating. The shares are currently priced at $115.34, and the $167.90 average target price implies a 45.5% gain on the one-year horizon. (See LSCC stock forecast .)

Microchip Technology Incorporated ( MCHP )

The second stock we'll look at here is another of the smaller chip makers. Microchip has been forging its global footprint in the industry since 1989, and today the Arizona-based company describes itself as 'a broadline supplier of semiconductors.' Microchip's goal in the field is to provide comprehensive solutions that address the multiple challenges of innovative design, emerging technologies, and durable end markets.

Microchip's core work can be described quite simply. The company designs, manufactures, sells, and supports a wide range of smart, connected, and secure semiconductor products that are used in an even wider range of applications. The firm's product lines include FPGAs, along with analog chips, power controllers, connectivity circuits, and clock and timing components and systems – and these are backed by a complete development ecosystem, capable of moving chips from design to final fabrication.

This company has put its print on multiple industries in the US, and is a vital supplier of high-end semiconductors in the US automotive industry, where the increasing sophistication of self-driving or electric-drive vehicles is generating increasing demand for top-end chips. Microchip is among the largest domestic suppliers of microcontroller chips in the US market. Globally, the company serves over 100,000 customers, in every industry from automotive to aerospace and defense to communications and computing.

Microchip reported its fiscal 1Q27 results on August 6, and in that report showed a quarterly revenue figure of $1.485 billion. This beat the estimates by over $26 million, and was up 38% year-over-year. Microchip's bottom line, reported as a non-GAAP diluted net income per common share of $0.76, was 6 cents per share better than had been forecast. The company's cash reserve at the end of the quarter totaled over $272 million.

Covering Microchip from BMO, top analyst Harsh Kumar is unabashedly bullish on the stock. The analyst, who is rated by TipRanks as #10 out of some 12,500 stock experts on Wall Street, says of the chip company, "We are buyers of MCHP given our view that increased factory utilization, supported by improving industrial and automotive demand will drive significant gross and operating margin expansion. We also like the company's position in networking where it has reemphasized data center switching. Additionally, we are enthused by MCHP's growing presence in the space and satellite market. We expect continued EPS beats and see the company outperforming through this economic cycle."

When he puts this into quantified terms, something investors can take home, Kumar gives MCHP an Outperform (Buy) rating – along with a $95 price target that suggests a one-year return for the stock of 29%. (To watch Kumar's track record, click here .)

Overall, MCHP gets a Moderate Buy consensus rating on the Street, based on 19 reviews that split to 14 Buys and 5 Holds. The stock is priced at $73.45 and its $106.44 average target price implies it will gain 45% by this time next year. (See MCHP stock forecast .)

（中央社記者何秀玲台北2026年8月31日電）台股今天下跌202.98點，收在46128.47點，成交值新台幣1兆2017.92億元。三大法人同步賣超，合計賣超267.55億元；其中，外資轉賣超143.92億元，終止連3日買超，外資賣超前3名皆為ETF，買超力積電 (6770) 居冠，達7.37萬張。

三大法人外資及陸資、投信、自營商今天同步賣超台股，其中，自營商賣超74.53億元，投信賣超49.1億元，外資及陸資賣超143.92億元

根據證交所統計，外資賣超前2名為主動中信台灣收益（00406A）3萬8860張、群益台灣加權正2（00685L）2萬6021張，其他依序為元大台灣50正2（00631L）、京元電子 (2449) 、元大台灣50 (0050) 。

外資買超前2名為力積電7萬3710張、友達 (2409) 4萬1264張，其他依序為台新新光金 (2887) 、台企銀 (2834) 、凱基金 (2883) 。

至於成為市場焦點的欣興電子 (3037) 今天股價跌停，不過外資及投信逆勢站在買方；其中，外資買超約2206張、投信買超42張，自營商則賣超約99張，三大法人合計買超約2149張。

資深證券分析師王兆立向中央社記者表示，台股今天開低主要受到美股走跌影響，費城半導體指數重挫，加上南韓股市同步走弱，使早盤賣壓較重；不過盤中低接買盤進場，指數跌幅收斂，以及MSCI季度調整今天收盤生效，尾盤受到相關權重調整資金影響，最後一盤出現較明顯的拉抬，指數跌幅進一步收斂。

展望後市，王兆立認為，台股短線要突破46500點仍有一定壓力，一方面輝達財報利多效應僅維持約一天，另一方面美國聯準會主席華許談話偏鷹派，市場對9月升息機率的預期已升至近6成，可能壓抑短線風險性資產表現。預期台股短線仍將維持大箱型震盪格局，走勢偏向拉回整理。（編輯：張良知）
